section.main.heading: Making a Victim Personal Statement
section.main.intro: This guidance is for when you experience a crime in England and Wales.
section.main.p1: You have the right to make a Victim Personal Statement, which tells the court how a crime has affected you. It is included when the judge or magistrates are deciding on the sentence for a defendant.
section.main.p2: This is different to your witness statement. It is for you to say how the crime has affected you, whether physically, emotionally, financially or in any other way.
section.main.p3: It can also be called a VPS or a 'Victim Impact Statement'.
section.when.heading: When you give the statement
section.when.p1: You can choose to give your Victim Personal Statement to the police when you report the crime, or up until the case goes to court.
section.when.p2: You can also make an updated statement until the case goes to court. It's important to remember that as a Victim Personal Statement is a legal document, even if you make a new one later on, any previous ones you have made are kept on record.
section.when.p3: You can also ask to read your Victim Personal Statement out in court if you want to.
section.how.heading: How the statement can help your case
section.how.p1: Your Victim Personal Statement helps the court, police, and prosecutors understand the emotional, physical, and financial effects the crime has had on you and your life.
section.how.p2: If a defendant is found guilty, the court will take your Victim Personal Statement into account, along with all the other evidence, when deciding on an appropriate sentence.
section.write.heading: How to write a Victim Personal Statement
section.write.p1: You can consider writing in your own words about how the crime has affected different parts of your life, such as your:
section.write.examplesIntro: For example, you might write about:
section.write.examples: an injury and its effects on your life
medical treatment or therapy you have had
how your quality of life has changed on a day-to-day basis
section.write.policeAdvice: You can get more advice and support to help you write your statement from the police.
section.write.whoCanWrite: A victim of crime must write their Victim Personal Statement themself. The law allows someone else to write it when the victim:
section.write.whoCanWriteList: is not able because of illness, injury, or mental health – a representative such as a close family member can write it
is aged under 18 – their parent or carer can write it, if appropriate
has died – a family member can write it
